1	// Command govflow is the DAO 治理提案与执行平台 entry point.
2	package main
3	
4	import (
5		"encoding/json"
6		"errors"
7		"flag"
8		"fmt"
9		"io"
10		"os"
11		"strings"
12	
13		"github.com/gzhysuiioo/govflow-proposals/govflow"
14		"github.com/gzhysuiioo/govflow-proposals/govflow/batchreg"
15	)
16	
17	const batchRegisterUsage = `usage: govflow batch-register --registry FILE --batch ID --product ID --quantity N --unit UNIT
18	run 'govflow help' for the full description and the registry file format.
19	`
20	
21	const batchImportUsage = `usage: govflow batch-import --registry FILE --input FILE
22	run 'govflow help' for the full description and the registry file format.
23	`
24	
25	func main() {
26		if err := run(os.Args[1:]); err != nil {
27			fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "govflow:", err)
28			var ue *usageError
29			if errors.As(err, &ue) {
30				fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, ue.usage)
31			}
32			os.Exit(1)
33		}
34	}
35	
36	type usageError struct {
37		msg   string
38		usage string
39	}
40	
41	func (e *usageError) Error() string { return e.msg }
42	
43	func run(args []string) error {
44		command := "demo"
45		if len(args) > 0 {
46			command = args[0]
47		}
48		switch command {
49		case "demo":
50			runDemo()
51			return nil
52		case "version":
53			fmt.Println("govflow 0.1.0")
54			return nil
55		case "help", "-h", "--help":
56			fmt.Print(rootUsage())
57			return nil
58		case "batch-register":
59			return runBatchRegister(args[1:], os.Stdout)
60		case "batch-import":
61			return runBatchImport(args[1:], os.Stdout)
62		default:
63			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "unknown command %q\n", command)
64			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, rootUsage())
65			os.Exit(2)
66			return nil
67		}
68	}
69	
70	func rootUsage() string {
71		return `govflow - DAO 治理提案与执行平台 / supply-chain batch registry
72	
73	usage:
74	  govflow                                  run the built-in demo (default)
75	  govflow demo                             run the built-in demo
76	  govflow version                          print the version
77	  govflow help                             show this help
78	  govflow batch-register --registry FILE \
79	      --batch ID --product ID --quantity N --unit UNIT
80	                                           register one supply-chain batch in
81	                                           the registry FILE (see below)
82	  govflow batch-import --registry FILE --input FILE
83	                                           register every batch listed in the
84	                                           JSON manifest FILE into the registry
85	                                           FILE, all records or none
86	
87	batch-register flags:
88	  --registry FILE   registry file to read and write (required)
89	  --batch ID        batch number; unique within one registry file (required)
90	  --product ID      product number the batch belongs to (required)
91	  --quantity N      positive decimal integer, digits 0-9 only, leading
92	                    zeros allowed, max 9223372036854775807 (required)
93	  --unit UNIT       measurement unit, e.g. kg or box (required)
94	
95	batch-import flags:
96	  --registry FILE   registry file to read and write (required)
97	  --input FILE      read-only JSON manifest (required); a non-empty array of
98	                    objects carrying exactly batch, product, quantity and
99	                    unit. Text fields must be non-blank after trimming, and
100	                    quantity must be a JSON integer from 1 to
101	                    9223372036854775807 (no strings, fractions or exponents)
102	
103	The whole manifest is rejected unless every record can be registered or
104	confirmed as a duplicate: a batch id already stored or seen earlier in the
105	manifest must match product, quantity and unit exactly, or none of the new
106	batches are saved and the error names the 1-based record position, the batch
107	id and the mismatching field(s). On success stdout contains one JSON object
108	whose results array keeps manifest order, each entry carrying the normalized
109	four fields plus status "created" or "duplicate"; new batches are appended
110	in first-occurrence order and an all-duplicate manifest leaves the registry
111	file byte-for-byte untouched.
112	
113	Batch, product and unit values have leading and trailing whitespace removed
114	and must be non-empty afterwards; interior characters and casing are kept
115	("B1" and "b1" are different batches). One invocation registers one batch.
116	
117	Batch, product and unit must be valid UTF-8 text in every source: command
118	line flags, import manifest records and stored registry records. A value
119	containing malformed UTF-8 bytes (or a JSON string holding a lone surrogate
120	escape such as "\ud800") is rejected and never replaced with the U+FFFD
121	replacement character, so distinct inputs cannot collapse onto one batch
122	id; the error names the parameter, or the manifest/registry file with the
123	1-based record position and field (plus the batch id only when it is itself
124	valid and unambiguous). The same rule applies to field NAMES in the JSON
125	files: a name with malformed bytes or a lone surrogate escape rejects the
126	whole operation with an invalid-field-name error naming the file (plus the
127	1-based record position, and the batch id when unambiguous, for record
128	level problems) — it is never reported as an unknown field under the
129	substituted text. A genuinely entered U+FFFD character is ordinary
130	text, non-ASCII ids (Chinese text, emoji, ...) are welcome, and a JSON
131	escape means the same text as the character written directly.
132	
133	On success stdout contains a single JSON object, e.g.
134	  {"batch":"B-001","product":"P-7","quantity":120,"unit":"kg","status":"created"}
135	status is "created" for a new record and "duplicate" when the same batch was
136	already registered with the identical product, quantity and unit; a duplicate
137	does not rewrite the file and is safe to retry. Registering an existing batch
138	with any different field is rejected; the error names the batch and the
139	mismatching field(s) and no record is changed.
140	
141	registry file format (UTF-8 JSON, human-inspectable):
142	  {
143	    "version": 1,
144	    "batches": [
145	      {"batch": "B-001", "product": "P-7", "quantity": 120, "unit": "kg"}
146	    ]
147	  }
148	A missing file is created on first registration, and a registry whose parent
149	directory does not yet exist is created together with that directory, as long
150	as the path never climbs back out of a directory it just descended into. The
151	registry path must name a FILE: a path ending in one or more path separators
152	("store/new.json/") or whose final component is "." or ".." ("store/new/.",
153	"store/new/..") spells a DIRECTORY location and is rejected outright, no
154	matter whether the location does not exist yet, already is a directory, or has
155	a regular file directly beneath the spelled name. The trailing directory
156	marker is never stripped to save a sibling plain file — "store/new.json/"
157	would otherwise create "store/new.json" and "store/new/." the plain file
158	"store/new", neither readable back through the path the user gave — no
159	missing parent directory is created, no registry or temporary file is left at
160	the stripped name, and an existing file, directory or symbolic link is never
161	replaced. The error quotes the registry path exactly as passed and states
162	that the target must be a file while this path denotes a directory; a "." or
163	".." in a MIDDLE path component ("store/./b.json") keeps resolving by the
164	ordinary rules.
165	A path that first passes through a directory that does not exist and then steps
166	back with ".." — store/missing/../batches.json while store/missing is absent —
167	names no file the way the filesystem resolves names and is rejected outright:
168	the missing directory is not created to make the path valid, the name left
169	after dropping the missing segment is not written (an existing registry there
170	is never overwritten), and no temporary file remains. A ".." that follows a
171	directory which really exists keeps working by the real directory relations.
172	The registry path may be a
173	symbolic link to an existing registry file: new batches are saved into the
174	linked file (a relative link target is resolved against the link's own
175	directory), the link itself is left untouched and the target keeps its
176	permissions. A symbolic link may also sit on a DIRECTORY component of the
177	path, together with "..": reads and saves resolve the path the way the
178	filesystem does, so with work/alias -> store/child the path
179	work/alias/../batches.json names store/batches.json, and a new batch is
180	appended to that real file rather than to a same-named file in the link's
181	parent directory. The temporary file is prepared in the real file's own
182	directory, so a read-only work directory (read and enter, but not create)
183	does not block the save and nothing is created under work; only an
184	unwritable real target directory rejects it. A link whose target does not
185	exist, or a loop of links, is rejected — the target is never created and
186	the link is never replaced. An
187	existing file that is empty, cannot be read in this format, or contains
188	several records with the same batch number is rejected outright and never
189	overwritten. "This format"
190	is strict: the root object must carry exactly version (the integer 1) and
191	batches (an array, empty allowed), each record exactly the four lowercase
192	fields batch, product, quantity and unit; missing, null, mistyped, unknown
193	or case-variant fields (Version, Batch, ...) are rejected, and so is any
194	field appearing twice in one object — even with identical values, even when
195	one spelling hides behind a JSON escape. The error names the file, the
196	field and the reason, plus the 1-based record position (and the batch id
197	when it is unambiguous) for record-level problems. Failures print
198	the reason to stderr and exit non-zero without touching the registry.
199	`
200	}
201	
202	func runBatchRegister(args []string, stdout io.Writer) error {
203		fs := flag.NewFlagSet("batch-register", flag.ContinueOnError)
204		fs.SetOutput(io.Discard)
205		registryPath := fs.String("registry", "", "registry `file` to read and write")
206		batchRaw := fs.String("batch", "", "batch number (unique within the registry)")
207		productRaw := fs.String("product", "", "product number")
208		quantityRaw := fs.String("quantity", "", "positive decimal integer quantity")
209		unitRaw := fs.String("unit", "", "measurement unit")
210		if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
211			if errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {
212				fmt.Fprint(stdout, rootUsage())
213				return nil
214			}
215			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
216		}
217		if fs.NArg() != 0 {
218			return &usageError{
219				msg:   fmt.Sprintf("batch-register: unexpected positional argument(s): %s", strings.Join(fs.Args(), " ")),
220				usage: batchRegisterUsage,
221			}
222		}
223	
224		// Missing or malformed input must never create or modify the registry
225		// file, so required flags are checked before reading or writing anything.
226		required := []struct {
227			name  string
228			value string
229		}{
230			{"--registry", *registryPath},
231			{"--batch", *batchRaw},
232			{"--product", *productRaw},
233			{"--quantity", *quantityRaw},
234			{"--unit", *unitRaw},
235		}
236		var missing []string
237		for _, f := range required {
238			if f.value == "" {
239				missing = append(missing, f.name)
240			}
241		}
242		if len(missing) > 0 {
243			return &usageError{
244				msg:   "batch-register: missing required flag(s): " + strings.Join(missing, ", "),
245				usage: batchRegisterUsage,
246			}
247		}
248	
249		batch, err := batchreg.NormalizeField(*batchRaw)
250		if err != nil {
251			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: invalid --batch: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
252		}
253		product, err := batchreg.NormalizeField(*productRaw)
254		if err != nil {
255			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: invalid --product: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
256		}
257		unit, err := batchreg.NormalizeField(*unitRaw)
258		if err != nil {
259			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: invalid --unit: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
260		}
261		quantity, err := batchreg.ParseQuantity(*quantityRaw)
262		if err != nil {
263			return &usageError{msg: "batch-register: invalid --quantity: " + err.Error(), usage: batchRegisterUsage}
264		}
265	
266		reg, existed, err := batchreg.Load(*registryPath)
267		if err != nil {
268			return err
269		}
270		outcome, err := batchreg.Register(reg, batchreg.Input{
271			Batch: batch, Product: product, Quantity: quantity, Unit: unit,
272		})
273		if err != nil {
274			return err
275		}
276		if outcome.Created {
277			if err := batchreg.Save(*registryPath, reg); err != nil {
278				if !existed {
279					// Nothing was registered before; drop any partial new file.
280					removePartialNewRegistry(*registryPath)
281				}
282				return err
283			}
284		}
285	
286		status := "duplicate"
287		if outcome.Created {
288			status = "created"
289		}
290		result := struct {
291			Batch    string `json:"batch"`
292			Product  string `json:"product"`
293			Quantity int64  `json:"quantity"`
294			Unit     string `json:"unit"`
295			Status   string `json:"status"`
296		}{
297			Batch:    outcome.Batch.Batch,
298			Product:  outcome.Batch.Product,
299			Quantity: outcome.Batch.Quantity,
300			Unit:     outcome.Batch.Unit,
301			Status:   status,
302		}
303		payload, err := json.Marshal(result)
304		if err != nil {
305			return err
306		}
307		_, err = fmt.Fprintln(stdout, string(payload))
308		return err
309	}
310	
311	func runBatchImport(args []string, stdout io.Writer) error {
312		fs := flag.NewFlagSet("batch-import", flag.ContinueOnError)
313		fs.SetOutput(io.Discard)
314		registryPath := fs.String("registry", "", "registry `file` to read and write")
315		inputPath := fs.String("input", "", "read-only JSON manifest `file` to import")
316		if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
317			if errors.Is(err, flag.ErrHelp) {
318				fmt.Fprint(stdout, rootUsage())
319				return nil
320			}
321			return &usageError{msg: "batch-import: " + err.Error(), usage: batchImportUsage}
322		}
323		if fs.NArg() != 0 {
324			return &usageError{
325				msg:   fmt.Sprintf("batch-import: unexpected positional argument(s): %s", strings.Join(fs.Args(), " ")),
326				usage: batchImportUsage,
327			}
328		}
329		if *registryPath == "" || *inputPath == "" {
330			var missing []string
331			if *registryPath == "" {
332				missing = append(missing, "--registry")
333			}
334			if *inputPath == "" {
335				missing = append(missing, "--input")
336			}
337			return &usageError{
338				msg:   "batch-import: missing required flag(s): " + strings.Join(missing, ", "),
339				usage: batchImportUsage,
340			}
341		}
342	
343		// The manifest is read-only and is parsed (and fully validated) before
344		// the registry is loaded or written, so bad input cannot touch it.
345		data, err := os.ReadFile(*inputPath)
346		if err != nil {
347			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: cannot read input file %q: %w", *inputPath, err)
348		}
349		inputs, err := batchreg.ParseManifest(data)
350		if err != nil {
351			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: invalid input file %q: %w", *inputPath, err)
352		}
353	
354		reg, existed, err := batchreg.Load(*registryPath)
355		if err != nil {
356			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
357		}
358		outcomes, err := batchreg.Import(reg, inputs)
359		if err != nil {
360			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
361		}
362	
363		type importResultJSON struct {
364			Batch    string `json:"batch"`
365			Product  string `json:"product"`
366			Quantity int64  `json:"quantity"`
367			Unit     string `json:"unit"`
368			Status   string `json:"status"`
369		}
370		results := make([]importResultJSON, len(outcomes))
371		anyCreated := false
372		for i, o := range outcomes {
373			status := "duplicate"
374			if o.Created {
375				status = "created"
376				anyCreated = true
377			}
378			results[i] = importResultJSON{
379				Batch:    o.Batch.Batch,
380				Product:  o.Batch.Product,
381				Quantity: o.Batch.Quantity,
382				Unit:     o.Batch.Unit,
383				Status:   status,
384			}
385		}
386	
387		// An all-duplicate manifest must leave bytes and mtime untouched, so the
388		// registry is written only when at least one record was newly created.
389		if anyCreated {
390			if err := batchreg.Save(*registryPath, reg); err != nil {
391				if !existed {
392					// The registry never existed before this import; drop any
393					// partial new file so a failed save leaves nothing behind.
394					removePartialNewRegistry(*registryPath)
395				}
396				return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
397			}
398		}
399	
400		payload, err := json.Marshal(struct {
401			Results []importResultJSON `json:"results"`
402		}{Results: results})
403		if err != nil {
404			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
405		}
406		_, err = fmt.Fprintln(stdout, string(payload))
407		if err != nil {
408			return fmt.Errorf("batch-import: %w", err)
409		}
410		return nil
411	}
412	
413	// removePartialNewRegistry drops a partially written new registry file after
414	// a failed first save. A symbolic link is never removed: the link is the
415	// user's pointer to the real registry file, not a partial creation of this
416	// run.
417	func removePartialNewRegistry(path string) {
418		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
419		if err != nil || info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
420			return
421		}
422		os.Remove(path)
423	}
424	
425	func runDemo() {
426		proposal := govflow.Proposal{ID: "gip-7", Title: "fund the audit workstream", State: "voting", Quorum: 1000,
427			TimelockEnd: 5000, Actions: []string{"transfer:audits:25000"}}
428		if err := govflow.Vote(&proposal, 700, true); err != nil {
429			fmt.Println("vote refused:", err)
430		}
431		if err := govflow.Vote(&proposal, 200, false); err != nil {
432			fmt.Println("vote refused:", err)
433		}
434		next := govflow.Tally(&proposal)
435		fmt.Printf("proposal=%s for=%d against=%d quorum=%d next=%s\n", proposal.ID, proposal.ForVotes, proposal.AgainstVotes, proposal.Quorum, next)
436		proposal.State = next
437		proposal.TimelockEnd = 400
438		fmt.Println("executable now:", govflow.Executable([]govflow.Proposal{proposal}, 1000))
439	}

1	package batchreg
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"path/filepath"
7		"strconv"
8		"strings"
9		"testing"
10	)
11	
12	// This file is the regression net for one narrow rule: when a single batch
13	// record carries BOTH an unknown field and a duplicated field, each on-disk
14	// source must reject it with a stable, specific reason — never a vague "the
15	// record is bad". The two sources deliberately report a different first
16	// problem:
17	//
18	//   - the registry file reports any duplicated field first (the first field
19	//     name whose SECOND occurrence appears earliest in the source), and only
20	//     reports the first unknown field when nothing is repeated;
21	//   - the import manifest reports the first anomaly in source order, so an
22	//     unknown member seen before the first repeat stays the reported problem
23	//     even when a duplicate follows it.
24	//
25	// Field names are compared after JSON decoding: a direct spelling and a legal
26	// \uXXXX escape of the same name are one member, while a normal field written
27	// once through an escape is perfectly legal. Errors keep the source file, the
28	// 1-based record position, the exact decoded field name, and the batch id
29	// (verbatim in the registry, trimmed in the manifest) only when exactly one
30	// valid batch member exists.
31	
32	// escKey renders an ASCII field name entirely as JSON \u00XX unicode escapes
33	// (escKey("x") == `x`), so the test JSON literally carries escaped key
34	// spellings that decode to the plain name. This is what proves comparison
35	// happens on the decoded text rather than the raw bytes.
36	func escKey(name string) string {
37		var b strings.Builder
38		for _, r := range name {
39			fmt.Fprintf(&b, `\u%04x`, r)
40		}
41		return b.String()
42	}
43	
44	var (
45		escProduct  = escKey("product")  // decodes to "product"
46		escBatch    = escKey("batch")    // decodes to "batch"
47		escSupplier = escKey("supplier") // decodes to "supplier"
48		escUnit     = escKey("unit")     // decodes to "unit"
49	)
50	
51	// legalMemberFaultRecord is one valid record placed before every offending
52	// record, so the reported position must be 2 — never the preceding good batch.
53	const legalMemberFaultRecord = `{"batch":"B1","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`
54	
55	type memberFaultSource string
56	
57	const (
58		faultFromRegistry memberFaultSource = "registry"
59		faultFromManifest memberFaultSource = "manifest"
60	)
61	
62	type memberFaultExpectation struct {
63		name   string
64		source memberFaultSource
65		// record is the offending JSON object, placed second after a legal record.
66		record string
67		field  string // exact decoded field name the error must carry
68		dup    bool   // true: duplicate reason; false: unknown-field reason
69		batch  string // batch id the error must cite; "" when it must cite none
70	}
71	
72	func memberFaultCases() []memberFaultExpectation {
73		return []memberFaultExpectation{
74			// The canonical divergence: an unknown supplier first, product
75			// repeated later. Registry names the duplicate; the manifest names
76			// the unknown field that appeared first.
77			{
78				"registry unknown supplier before duplicate product reports product duplicate",
79				faultFromRegistry,
80				`{"batch":"B2","supplier":"S","product":"P","product":"Q","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
81				"product", true, "B2",
82			},
83			{
84				"manifest unknown supplier before duplicate product reports supplier unknown",
85				faultFromManifest,
86				`{"batch":"B2","supplier":"S","product":"P","product":"Q","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
87				"supplier", false, "B2",
88			},
89			// Same record with the product repeat moved ahead of the unknown:
90			// both sources report the duplicate.
91			{
92				"registry duplicate product ahead of unknown reports product duplicate",
93				faultFromRegistry,
94				`{"batch":"B2","product":"P","product":"Q","quantity":1,"unit":"kg","supplier":"S"}`,
95				"product", true, "B2",
96			},
97			{
98				"manifest duplicate product ahead of unknown reports product duplicate",
99				faultFromManifest,
100				`{"batch":"B2","product":"P","product":"Q","quantity":1,"unit":"kg","supplier":"S"}`,
101				"product", true, "B2",
102			},
103			// One record contrasting both rules: the unknown supplier appears
104			// first, but unit's second occurrence comes before product's second.
105			// The registry reports the duplicate whose second occurrence is
106			// earliest (unit); the manifest keeps source order and reports the
107			// unknown supplier.
108			{
109				"registry reports earliest second occurrence (unit) over unknown and later product repeat",
110				faultFromRegistry,
111				`{"batch":"B2","product":"P","unit":"kg","supplier":"S","unit":"g","product":"Q","quantity":1}`,
112				"unit", true, "B2",
113			},
114			{
115				"manifest reports first unknown and is not moved by either later repeat",
116				faultFromManifest,
117				`{"batch":"B2","product":"P","unit":"kg","supplier":"S","unit":"g","product":"Q","quantity":1}`,
118				"supplier", false, "B2",
119			},
120			// Two fields repeated and no unknown: the registry picks the one
121			// whose second occurrence happens first.
122			{
123				"registry tie-break: product repeats before unit repeats",
124				faultFromRegistry,
125				`{"batch":"B2","product":"P","unit":"kg","quantity":1,"product":"P","unit":"kg"}`,
126				"product", true, "B2",
127			},
128			{
129				"registry tie-break: unit repeats before product repeats",
130				faultFromRegistry,
131				`{"batch":"B2","product":"P","unit":"kg","quantity":1,"unit":"kg","product":"P"}`,
132				"unit", true, "B2",
133			},
134			// No duplicate anywhere: the registry reports the first unknown
135			// member in source order.
136			{
137				"registry without duplicates reports first unknown field",
138				faultFromRegistry,
139				`{"batch":"B2","alpha":1,"beta":2,"product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
140				"alpha", false, "B2",
141			},
142			// The manifest reports the first repeat and is not moved by a later
143			// unknown.
144			{
145				"manifest reports the first repeat and ignores a later unknown",
146				faultFromManifest,
147				`{"batch":"B2","product":"P","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg","zz":1,"yy":2}`,
148				"product", true, "B2",
149			},
150			// Names are judged on the decoded text: an escaped respelling is the
151			// same member as the directly written one — a duplicate even when the
152			// two values are identical — while an escape used alone stays legal
153			// (covered by the acceptance test below).
154			{
155				"registry escaped product spelling duplicates direct name with equal values",
156				faultFromRegistry,
157				`{"batch":"B2","` + escProduct + `":"P","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
158				"product", true, "B2",
159			},
160			{
161				"manifest escaped product spelling duplicates direct name with equal values",
162				faultFromManifest,
163				`{"batch":"B2","` + escProduct + `":"P","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
164				"product", true, "B2",
165			},
166			{
167				"registry direct name duplicates escaped spelling with different values",
168				faultFromRegistry,
169				`{"batch":"B2","product":"P","` + escProduct + `":"Q","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
170				"product", true, "B2",
171			},
172			// An escaped unknown name is reported under its decoded text, and the
173			// registry still prefers a later duplicate to that earlier unknown.
174			{
175				"registry escaped unknown plus later duplicate reports the duplicate",
176				faultFromRegistry,
177				`{"batch":"B2","` + escSupplier + `":"S","product":"P","product":"Q","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
178				"product", true, "B2",
179			},
180			{
181				"manifest escaped unknown name is reported decoded",
182				faultFromManifest,
183				`{"batch":"B2","` + escSupplier + `":"S","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
184				"supplier", false, "B2",
185			},
186			// An escaped repeat participates in the earliest-second-occurrence
187			// tie-break: the escaped unit repeat lands before the product repeat.
188			{
189				"registry escaped unit repeat outranks a later product repeat",
190				faultFromRegistry,
191				`{"batch":"B2","product":"P","unit":"kg","` + escUnit + `":"kg","product":"P","quantity":1}`,
192				"unit", true, "B2",
193			},
194			// The single legal batch member may sit after the offending field;
195			// its position is irrelevant to whether it identifies the record.
196			{
197				"registry cites batch id written after the offending fields",
198				faultFromRegistry,
199				`{"supplier":"S","product":"P","product":"Q","quantity":1,"unit":"kg","batch":"B9"}`,
200				"product", true, "B9",
201			},
202			{
203				"manifest cites batch id written after the offending field",
204				faultFromManifest,
205				`{"supplier":"S","batch":"B9","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
206				"supplier", false, "B9",
207			},
208			// The registry keeps the batch text verbatim; the manifest trims it.
209			{
210				"registry keeps the padded batch id verbatim",
211				faultFromRegistry,
212				`{"batch":" B2 ","supplier":"S","product":"P","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
213				"product", true, " B2 ",
214			},
215			{
216				"manifest normalizes the padded batch id",
217				faultFromManifest,
218				`{"batch":" B2 ","supplier":"S","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`,
219				"supplier", false, "B2",
220			},
221			// A duplicated batch member — even with two identical values —
222			// identifies no record: neither source may pick one value to name it.
223			{
224				"registry duplicated batch with equal values cites no id",
225				faultFromRegistry,
226				`{"batch":"B2","batch":"B2","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg","supplier":"S"}`,
227				"batch", true, "",
228			},
229			{
230				"manifest duplicated batch with equal values cites no id",
231				faultFromManifest,
232				`{"batch":"B2","batch":"B2","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg","supplier":"S"}`,
233				"batch", true, "",
234			},
235			// A duplicated batch hidden behind an escape is equally unidentifiable,
236			// even though an unknown member is present too (duplicate still wins
237			// in the registry; the first repeat is the batch in the manifest).
238			{
239				"registry escaped duplicated batch cites no id over a later unknown",
240				faultFromRegistry,
241				`{"batch":"B2","` + escBatch + `":"B2","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg","supplier":"S"}`,
242				"batch", true, "",
243			},
244		}
245	}
246	
247	// TestRecordMemberFaultPrecedenceAcrossSources drives one offending record
248	// through the actual reader of each source and asserts the full error shape:
249	// position counted from the very first record, the exact decoded field name,
250	// a reason that distinguishes "duplicate" from "unknown" (not mere rejection),
251	// and the batch id exactly under that source's text policy.
252	func TestRecordMemberFaultPrecedenceAcrossSources(t *testing.T) {
253		for _, tc := range memberFaultCases() {
254			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
255				switch tc.source {
256				case faultFromRegistry:
257					path := memberFaultRegistryFile(t, `{"version":1,"batches":[`+legalMemberFaultRecord+`,`+tc.record+`]}`)
258					_, _, err := Load(path)
259					var fe *FormatError
260					if !errors.As(err, &fe) {
261						t.Fatalf("expected FormatError, got %v", err)
262					}
263					if fe.Position != 2 {
264						t.Errorf("position=%d, want 2: the legal first record must not be blamed", fe.Position)
265					}
266					if fe.Field != tc.field {
267						t.Errorf("field=%q, want %q (error: %v)", fe.Field, tc.field, err)
268					}
269					if fe.Batch != tc.batch {
270						t.Errorf("batch=%q, want %q (error: %v)", fe.Batch, tc.batch, err)
271					}
272					assertMemberFaultReason(t, err.Error(), tc)
273				case faultFromManifest:
274					content := []byte(`[` + legalMemberFaultRecord + `,` + tc.record + `]`)
275					inputs, err := ParseManifest(content)
276					var re *ManifestRecordError
277					if !errors.As(err, &re) {
278						t.Fatalf("expected ManifestRecordError, got %v", err)
279					}
280					if inputs != nil {
281						t.Fatalf("a rejected manifest must yield no inputs, got %+v", inputs)
282					}
283					if re.Position != 2 {
284						t.Errorf("position=%d, want 2: the legal first record must not be blamed", re.Position)
285					}
286					if re.Batch != tc.batch {
287						t.Errorf("batch=%q, want %q (error: %v)", re.Batch, tc.batch, err)
288					}
289					assertMemberFaultReason(t, err.Error(), tc)
290				default:
291					t.Fatalf("unknown source %q", tc.source)
292				}
293			})
294		}
295	}
296	
297	// assertMemberFaultReason checks that the wording distinguishes the two fault
298	// kinds, quotes the exact field name, and cites/omits the batch id as
299	// required.
300	func assertMemberFaultReason(t *testing.T, msg string, tc memberFaultExpectation) {
301		t.Helper()
302		if tc.dup {
303			if !strings.Contains(msg, "more than once") {
304				t.Errorf("error must report a DUPLICATE field %q: %v", tc.field, msg)
305			}
306			if strings.Contains(msg, "unknown field") {
307				t.Errorf("error must not mislabel the duplicate as unknown: %v", msg)
308			}
309		} else {
310			if !strings.Contains(msg, "unknown field") {
311				t.Errorf("error must report an UNKNOWN field %q: %v", tc.field, msg)
312			}
313			if strings.Contains(msg, "more than once") {
314				t.Errorf("error must not mislabel the unknown field as a duplicate: %v", msg)
315			}
316		}
317		if !strings.Contains(msg, strconv.Quote(tc.field)) {
318			t.Errorf("error must name the exact decoded field %q: %v", tc.field, msg)
319		}
320		if tc.batch != "" {
321			if !strings.Contains(msg, "(batch "+strconv.Quote(tc.batch)+")") {
322				t.Errorf("error must cite batch %q: %v", tc.batch, msg)
323			}
324		} else if strings.Contains(msg, "(batch \"") {
325			t.Errorf("error must not invent a batch id: %v", msg)
326		}
327	}
328	
329	// memberFaultRegistryFile writes content into a fresh registry file and
330	// returns its path.
331	func memberFaultRegistryFile(t *testing.T, content string) string {
332		t.Helper()
333		path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "registry.json")
334		writeRegistry(t, path, content)
335		return path
336	}
337	
338	// TestEscapedFieldNamesAcceptedWhenNotRepeated is the acceptance mirror of the
339	// duplicate-escape cases: escaping alone is never an error. Every normal field
340	// written once through a legal \uXXXX escape must load and parse normally —
341	// otherwise "every escaped name is wrong" would pass the rejection-only
342	// assertions above while breaking the public format.
343	func TestEscapedFieldNamesAcceptedWhenNotRepeated(t *testing.T) {
344		t.Run("registry accepts escaped member names", func(t *testing.T) {
345			content := `{"version":1,"batches":[` + legalMemberFaultRecord + `,
346				{"` + escBatch + `":"B2","` + escProduct + `":"P 8","quantity":2,"` + escUnit + `":"kg"}]}`
347			reg, existed, err := Load(memberFaultRegistryFile(t, content))
348			if err != nil {
349				t.Fatalf("legal escaped member names must load: %v", err)
350			}
351			if !existed || len(reg.Batches) != 2 {
352				t.Fatalf("existed=%v batches=%+v", existed, reg.Batches)
353			}
354			want := Batch{Batch: "B2", Product: "P 8", Quantity: 2, Unit: "kg"}
355			if reg.Batches[1] != want {
356				t.Fatalf("escaped record decoded as %+v, want %+v", reg.Batches[1], want)
357			}
358			// The escaped record is genuinely stored: re-registering its exact
359			// values confirms a duplicate rather than failing on the spellings.
360			if out, err := Register(reg, Input{Batch: "B2", Product: "P 8", Quantity: 2, Unit: "kg"}); err != nil || out.Created {
361				t.Fatalf("escaped-name record should be a stored, confirmable record: %+v err=%v", out, err)
362			}
363		})
364	
365		t.Run("manifest accepts, decodes and trims escaped member names", func(t *testing.T) {
366			content := []byte(`[` + legalMemberFaultRecord + `,
367				{"` + escBatch + `":" B2 ","` + escProduct + `":"P 8","quantity":2,"` + escUnit + `":"kg"}]`)
368			inputs, err := ParseManifest(content)
369			if err != nil {
370				t.Fatalf("legal escaped member names must parse: %v", err)
371			}
372			if len(inputs) != 2 {
373				t.Fatalf("got %d inputs, want 2", len(inputs))
374			}
375			want := Input{Batch: "B2", Product: "P 8", Quantity: 2, Unit: "kg"}
376			if inputs[1] != want {
377				t.Fatalf("escaped manifest record decoded as %+v, want %+v", inputs[1], want)
378			}
379			// And the all-legal control actually imports — rejection must not be
380			// the only outcome under test.
381			reg := &Registry{Version: FormatVersion}
382			out, err := Import(reg, inputs)
383			if err != nil {
384				t.Fatalf("legal control manifest must import: %v", err)
385			}
386			if len(out) != 2 || !out[0].Created || !out[1].Created {
387				t.Fatalf("unexpected import outcomes: %+v", out)
388			}
389			if len(reg.Batches) != 2 || reg.Batches[1].Batch != "B2" {
390				t.Fatalf("registry should hold both legal batches: %+v", reg.Batches)
391			}
392		})
393	}
394	
395	// TestLegalControlRecordStillReadsThroughBothSources pairs the same good
396	// record that precedes every bad one above with a repaired second record: the
397	// bad combination must fail, but the repaired manifest must parse and import
398	// cleanly and the repaired registry must load. This stops a blanket-reject
399	// implementation from masquerading as the guarantee.
400	func TestLegalControlRecordStillReadsThroughBothSources(t *testing.T) {
401		repaired := `{"batch":"B2","product":"P","quantity":1,"unit":"kg"}`
402	
403		t.Run("repaired registry loads and keeps both records", func(t *testing.T) {
404			content := `{"version":1,"batches":[` + legalMemberFaultRecord + `,` + repaired + `]}`
405			reg, existed, err := Load(memberFaultRegistryFile(t, content))
406			if err != nil {
407				t.Fatalf("the repaired registry must load: %v", err)
408			}
409			if !existed || len(reg.Batches) != 2 || reg.Batches[0].Batch != "B1" || reg.Batches[1].Batch != "B2" {
410				t.Fatalf("unexpected registry: %+v", reg.Batches)
411			}
412		})
413	
414		t.Run("repaired manifest parses, imports and confirms repeats", func(t *testing.T) {
415			content := []byte(`[` + legalMemberFaultRecord + `,` + repaired + `,` + repaired + `]`)
416			inputs, err := ParseManifest(content)
417			if err != nil {
418				t.Fatalf("the repaired manifest must parse: %v", err)
419			}
420			reg := &Registry{Version: FormatVersion, Batches: []Batch{
421				{Batch: "B1", Product: "P", Quantity: 1, Unit: "kg"},
422			}}
423			out, err := Import(reg, inputs)
424			if err != nil {
425				t.Fatalf("the repaired manifest must import: %v", err)
426			}
427			wantCreated := []bool{false, true, false} // B1 stored, B2 created, B2 repeat confirmed
428			if len(out) != len(wantCreated) {
429				t.Fatalf("got %d outcomes, want %d", len(out), len(wantCreated))
430			}
431			for i, want := range wantCreated {
432				if out[i].Created != want {
433					t.Errorf("record %d created=%v, want %v", i+1, out[i].Created, want)
434				}
435			}
436			if len(reg.Batches) != 2 {
437				t.Fatalf("registry should keep B1 and add B2 once: %+v", reg.Batches)
438			}

## 做了什么

读取（`checkRegistryPathReachable`，供 `Load` 用）和保存（`resolveRegistryTarget`，供 `Save` 用）此前各自维护了一段几乎相同的逻辑：用 `rawParent` 逐段剥离路径、对每个前缀 `os.Lstat`、找到最长存在前缀并判断是否符号链接。现在抽取为一个共享函数：

- **`longestExistingRegistryPrefix(path)`** 只负责爬升这一件事，返回最长存在前缀（保持用户原始拼写、不做词法清理）、该前缀是否为符号链接、尚不存在的原始组件尾部 `tail`，以及爬升中遇到的首个非 `not-exist` 的 Lstat 错误。它只调用 `Lstat`，不创建任何东西、不改链接。
- **`checkRegistryPathReachable`**（读）基于结果：前缀是无法解析的符号链接才拒绝（`EvalSymlinks` 失败 → 原有 `errUnreachablePathLink`）；缺失目录后接 `..` 仍按普通缺失文件放行；非 ENOENT 错误留给后续读取自己报。
- **`resolveRegistryTarget`**（写）基于同一份结果：非 ENOENT 错误立即拒绝、缺失目录后接 `..` 的逃逸仍拒绝（`errEscapeThroughMissingDir`）、悬空/成环链接仍拒绝，然后物理解析前缀并原样拼接缺失组件，保证临时文件与 rename 落在真实目标目录。

## 刻意保留的读/写差异

- `store/missing/../b.json`：读返回空的第 1 版登记表（`existed=false`），写拒绝；
- 悬空文件/目录链接、链接成环：读写都拒绝，错误类型、原始路径与原因文案不变，不返回空表、不建目标、不替换链接；
- 目录链接后接 `..` 按真实目录关系解析（`work/alias/../b.json` → `store/b.json`），相对链接目标仍以链接所在目录为准；
- 末尾分隔符/`.`/`..` 的 `DirectoryPathError` 仍在接触文件系统之前返回；
- 首次登记缺父目录仍可由 Save 创建，链接目录不可写、真实目标目录可写时保存仍成功且不在链接旁留临时文件。
